intended_object: For an R-algebra map φ : A → B, the induced R-algebra homomorphism A⟦X⟧ → B⟦X⟧ that applies φ to each coefficient, ∑ aₙXⁿ ↦ ∑ φ(aₙ)Xⁿ. This comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
`PowerSeries A` is by definition `MvPowerSeries Unit A`. So the definition is the same as `MvPowerSeries.mapAlgHom φ` with σ = Unit. That map is `MvPowerSeries.map φ`, which applies φ to every coefficient, bundled with the proof that it commutes with the algebra maps from R. This is exactly the change-of-coefficients map, as an algebra homomorphism.

The generality is the natural one. R is a commutative semiring and A, B are possibly noncommutative semirings that are R-algebras; no other hypotheses are used.

The multivariate definition `MvPowerSeries.mapAlgHom` is not a reason to call this one too narrow. It is the general version, and this definition is just its standard one-variable specialization, in the same way that `PowerSeries.map` relates to `MvPowerSeries.map`.
